caption.en: Using the psychrometric chart

alt.ru: Переход от двух показаний термогигрометра к GPP, точке росы и давлению пара, а также два основных применения
alt.en: Flow from two thermo-hygrometer readings to GPP, dew point and vapour pressure, plus the two main uses

s1-psychrometric-use.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 380" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">
<rect width="720" height="380" fill="#fff"/>
<text x="360" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Using the Psychrometric Chart</text>
<defs><marker id="pc" markerWidth="10" markerHeight="10" refX="8" refY="3" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L9,3 L0,6 z" fill="#12263a"/></marker></defs>
<rect x="30" y="46" width="300" height="60" rx="8" fill="#e8f1f8" stroke="#1b6ca8" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="180" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#1b6ca8">Take two readings with a thermo-hygrometer</text>
<text x="180" y="92" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">dry bulb temperature  +  relative humidity</text>
<line x1="180" y1="108" x2="180" y2="130" stroke="#12263a" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#pc)"/>
<rect x="30" y="134" width="300" height="76" rx="8" fill="#e7f3ec" stroke="#2e7d4f" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="180" y="156" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#12263a">Temperature = the air’s CAPACITY to hold moisture</text>
<text x="180" y="176" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#12263a">RH = the RELATIVE amount of moisture present</text>
<text x="180" y="198" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">Chart then gives GPP (g/kg), dew point, vapour pressure</text>
<rect x="356" y="46" width="334" height="164" rx="8" fill="#f7f9fb" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="523" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Three specific measures, all directly related</text>
<rect x="376" y="84" width="290" height="30" rx="4" fill="#e8f1f8" stroke="#1b6ca8"/>
<text x="521" y="104" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#12263a">HUMIDITY RATIO — GPP (g/kg)</text>
<rect x="376" y="120" width="290" height="30" rx="4" fill="#e8f1f8" stroke="#1b6ca8"/>
<text x="521" y="140" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#12263a">DEW POINT</text>
<rect x="376" y="156" width="290" height="30" rx="4" fill="#e8f1f8" stroke="#1b6ca8"/>
<text x="521" y="176" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#12263a">VAPOUR PRESSURE</text>
<text x="523" y="202" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">When GPP goes down, dew point and vapour pressure go down too</text>
<rect x="30" y="224" width="660" height="70" rx="8" fill="#fdf6e3" stroke="#c9a227" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="360" y="246" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#a5851f">Use 1 — can outdoor air be used for drying?</text>
<text x="360" y="266" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">Compare outdoor GPP with indoor GPP. Outdoor air is used ONLY when the outdoor GPP is LOWER.</text>
<text x="360" y="284" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">If it is not, the outdoor air is wetter than the indoor air and is not used.</text>
<rect x="30" y="304" width="660" height="66" rx="8" fill="#fbeee9" stroke="#d1491c" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="360" y="326" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">Use 2 — what happens when the air is heated or cooled?</text>
<text x="360" y="346" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">Heating outdoor air as it enters: GPP (g/kg) stays THE SAME, relative humidity DECREASES.</text>
<text x="360" y="364" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">RH alone never defines the water content of air unless the temperature is given.</text>
</svg>

caption.ru: Открытые, закрытые и комбинированные системы сушки
caption.en: Open, closed and combination drying systems

alt.ru: Три панели систем и трёхшаговый порядок выбора
alt.en: Three system panels and the three-step decision process

s1-drying-systems.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 380" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">
<rect width="720" height="380" fill="#fff"/>
<text x="360" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Open, Closed and Combination Drying Systems</text>
<rect x="16" y="44" width="224" height="126" rx="8" fill="#e7f3ec" stroke="#2e7d4f" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="128" y="68" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">OPEN</text>
<text x="128" y="92" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">Intentionally using outdoor air</text>
<text x="128" y="108" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">to lower indoor humidity, with</text>
<text x="128" y="124" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">NO mechanical dehumidification</text>
<text x="128" y="148" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">ventilation fans · windows wide</text>
<text x="128" y="162" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">air movers · heat and air exchange</text>
<rect x="248" y="44" width="224" height="126" rx="8" fill="#e8f1f8" stroke="#1b6ca8" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="360" y="68" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#1b6ca8">CLOSED</text>
<text x="360" y="92" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">Mechanical dehumidification</text>
<text x="360" y="108" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">ONLY, with the area isolated</text>
<text x="360" y="124" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">from outside air</text>
<text x="360" y="150" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">make sure ventilation fans and fresh</text>
<text x="360" y="164" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">air ventilation systems are closed</text>
<rect x="480" y="44" width="224" height="126" rx="8" fill="#fdf6e3" stroke="#c9a227" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="592" y="68" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#a5851f">COMBINATION</text>
<text x="592" y="92" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">Some outdoor air combined</text>
<text x="592" y="108" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">with mechanical</text>
<text x="592" y="124" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">dehumidification</text>
<text x="592" y="150" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">cold outdoor air must be paired with</text>
<text x="592" y="164" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">adequate heating</text>
<text x="360" y="198" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Deciding which system to use</text>
<rect x="16" y="210" width="688" height="42" rx="6" fill="#f7f9fb" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="34" y="236" font-size="12" fill="#12263a"><tspan font-weight="bold">1.</tspan>  Compare the moisture content of indoor and outdoor air. If the air outside is wetter (higher humidity ratio) → CLOSED system.</text>
<rect x="16" y="256" width="688" height="42" rx="6" fill="#f7f9fb" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="34" y="282" font-size="12" fill="#12263a"><tspan font-weight="bold">2.</tspan>  Consider air temperature. Outside air below 70°F (21°C) → CLOSED, or added heat with a COMBINATION system.</text>
<rect x="16" y="302" width="688" height="42" rx="6" fill="#f7f9fb" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="34" y="328" font-size="12" fill="#12263a"><tspan font-weight="bold">3.</tspan>  Consider dew point, building security, changing weather, customer preference and other factors ruling out open drying.</text>
<text x="360" y="364" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-style="italic" fill="#d1491c">Whichever system is used, monitor the environment frequently and modify the system as conditions change</text>
</svg>

caption.en: Stages of drying and the drying rate

alt.ru: Кривая падающей скорости испарения со стадиями постоянной и падающей скорости и их формулами
alt.en: Curve of falling evaporation rate with the constant rate and falling rate phases and their formulas

s1-drying-stages.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 380" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">
<rect width="720" height="380" fill="#fff"/>
<text x="360" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Stages of Drying and the Drying Rate</text>
<polyline points="60,120 150,124 230,150 330,208 450,244 600,262 680,268" fill="none" stroke="#1b6ca8" stroke-width="3"/>
<line x1="60" y1="96" x2="60" y2="284" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<line x1="60" y1="284" x2="684" y2="284" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="36" y="190" font-size="11" fill="#555" transform="rotate(-90 36,190)">evaporation rate</text>
<text x="372" y="302" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#555">time</text>
<line x1="215" y1="96" x2="215" y2="284" stroke="#d1491c" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="5,4"/>
<rect x="66" y="52" width="146" height="40" rx="6" fill="#e7f3ec" stroke="#2e7d4f" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="139" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">STAGE 1</text>
<text x="139" y="86" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">“Constant Rate”</text>
<rect x="222" y="52" width="460" height="40" rx="6" fill="#fbeee9" stroke="#d1491c" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="452" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">STAGES 2 and 3</text>
<text x="452" y="86" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">“Falling Rate”</text>
<rect x="16" y="312" width="330" height="60" rx="8" fill="#e7f3ec" stroke="#2e7d4f" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="181" y="332" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">Surface water and free water near the surface</text>
<text x="181" y="348" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">Large airflow + moderate temperature and humidity</text>
<text x="181" y="366" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">Evaporation = Airflow × Vapour Pressure Differential</text>
<rect x="360" y="312" width="344" height="60" rx="8" fill="#fbeee9" stroke="#d1491c" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="532" y="330" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Free water migrates to the surface, bound water diffuses as vapour</text>
<text x="532" y="346" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Evaporation happens deeper in the material; air speed loses relevance</text>
<text x="532" y="366" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">Evaporation = Vapour Pressure Differential</text>
<text x="452" y="130" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">Variables now: porosity and permeability, the hygroscopic</text>
<text x="452" y="146" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">nature of the material, distribution and depth of the water</text>
<text x="452" y="174" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Of the three factors researchers agree on — airflow,</text>
<text x="452" y="190" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">moisture transport, pressure differential — only</text>
<text x="452" y="206" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">PRESSURE DIFFERENTIAL can still be manipulated</text>
<text x="452" y="232" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="#555">airflow’s influence diminishes; moisture transport is a property</text>
<text x="452" y="246" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="#555">of the material that cannot be changed without damaging it</text>
</svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 740 390" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">
<rect width="740" height="390" fill="#fff"/>
<text x="370" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Dehumidifier Types — When to Use Which</text>
<g>
<rect x="16" y="44" width="230" height="222" rx="8" fill="#f7f9fb" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="131" y="68" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#5d6a73">CONVENTIONAL REFRIGERANT</text>
<text x="131" y="92" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Removes water by CONDENSATION</text>
<text x="131" y="108" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">on a cold coil below dew point</text>
<text x="131" y="132" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Works best 70–90°F (21–32°C)</text>
<text x="131" y="156" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">More efficient in HIGHER humidity</text>
<text x="131" y="180" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">Lowers to about 40% RH</text>
<text x="131" y="196" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">or about 55 GPP</text>
<text x="131" y="220" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">NOT adequate for Class 4 losses</text>
<text x="131" y="234" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">with large amounts of bound water</text>
<text x="131" y="256" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">Use for simple/small losses or as backup</text>
</g>
<g>
<rect x="256" y="44" width="230" height="222" rx="8" fill="#e8f1f8" stroke="#1b6ca8" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="371" y="68" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#1b6ca8">LOW GRAIN REFRIGERANT (LGR)</text>
<text x="371" y="92" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">A pre-cooling device supplies the</text>
<text x="371" y="108" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">unit with cooler air to process</text>
<text x="371" y="132" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Also best 70–90°F (21–32°C)</text>
<text x="371" y="156" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Works in high humidity AND in</text>
<text x="371" y="170" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">drier conditions; more energy efficient</text>
<text x="371" y="194" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#1b6ca8">Continues down to 34 GPP</text>
<text x="371" y="218" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Pre-cooling: heat pipe · thermal</text>
<text x="371" y="232" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">siphon · air-to-air heat exchanger</text>
<text x="371" y="256" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">The best choice for most drying situations</text>
</g>
<g>
<rect x="496" y="44" width="230" height="222" rx="8" fill="#e7f3ec" stroke="#2e7d4f" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="611" y="68" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">DESICCANT</text>
<text x="611" y="92" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Uses CHEMICAL ATTRACTION, not</text>
<text x="611" y="108" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">condensation — a silica gel rotor</text>
<text x="611" y="132" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Best in COOL and/or DRY air</text>
<text x="611" y="156" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Not limited by low dew point;</text>
<text x="611" y="172" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">produces the LOWEST vapour</text>
<text x="611" y="188" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">pressure of any dehumidifier</text>
<text x="611" y="212" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">No collection pan — damp</text>
<text x="611" y="226" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">reactivation air is vented outside</text>
<text x="611" y="250" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">Use for difficult Class 4 losses, or when</text>
<text x="611" y="262" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">the structure cannot be warmed for LGRs</text>
</g>
<rect x="16" y="278" width="710" height="100" rx="8" fill="#fdf6e3" stroke="#c9a227" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="371" y="300" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#a5851f">Refrigerant dehumidifier — key components</text>
<text x="34" y="324" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a"><tspan font-weight="bold">Cold (evaporator) coil</tspan> — where water condenses; typically 20–30°F below the dew point of the ambient air</text>
<text x="34" y="344" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a"><tspan font-weight="bold">Hot (condenser) coil</tspan> — purges waste heat, making the exiting air “thirstier”  ·  <tspan font-weight="bold">Compressor</tspan> — pressurises the refrigerant</text>
<text x="34" y="364" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a"><tspan font-weight="bold">Capillary tube</tspan> — maintains the pressure difference  ·  <tspan font-weight="bold">Defrost mechanism</tspan> — melts ice when the cold coil drops below 32°F (0°C)</text>
</svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 360" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">
<rect width="720" height="360" fill="#fff"/>
<text x="360" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Desiccant Dehumidifier — Airflow Through a “Three-Hole” Unit</text>
<defs><marker id="da" markerWidth="10" markerHeight="10" refX="8" refY="3" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L9,3 L0,6 z" fill="#12263a"/></marker></defs>
<rect x="250" y="80" width="220" height="170" rx="8" fill="#f7f9fb" stroke="#12263a" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<circle cx="330" cy="150" r="46" fill="#e7f3ec" stroke="#2e7d4f" stroke-width="3"/>
<g stroke="#2e7d4f" stroke-width="1.2">
<line x1="292" y1="130" x2="368" y2="130"/><line x1="288" y1="150" x2="372" y2="150"/><line x1="292" y1="170" x2="368" y2="170"/>
<line x1="310" y1="110" x2="310" y2="190"/><line x1="330" y1="106" x2="330" y2="194"/><line x1="350" y1="110" x2="350" y2="190"/>
</g>
<text x="330" y="216" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">DESICCANT WHEEL</text>
<text x="330" y="232" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">silica gel rotor, rotates slowly</text>
<rect x="412" y="104" width="42" height="34" rx="4" fill="#d1491c"/>
<text x="433" y="126" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#fff">HEAT</text>
<text x="433" y="152" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="#12263a">boosts the</text>
<text x="433" y="164" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="#12263a">reactivation air</text>
<line x1="120" y1="150" x2="244" y2="150" stroke="#1b6ca8" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#da)"/>
<text x="182" y="138" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#1b6ca8">PROCESS AIR IN</text>
<text x="182" y="168" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">75–100% of airflow; has a filter</text>
<text x="182" y="182" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">supply COOL, DRY air for best performance</text>
<line x1="476" y1="226" x2="600" y2="226" stroke="#2e7d4f" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#da)"/>
<text x="538" y="214" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">PROCESS AIR OUT — 75%</text>
<text x="538" y="244" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">warm, DRY processed air</text>
<text x="538" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">ducted into the affected area</text>
<line x1="476" y1="104" x2="600" y2="104" stroke="#d1491c" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#da)"/>
<text x="538" y="92" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">REACTIVATION AIR OUT — 25%</text>
<text x="538" y="122" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">extremely warm, HUMID air</text>
<text x="538" y="136" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">normally exhausted OUTSIDE the building</text>
<rect x="16" y="278" width="688" height="70" rx="8" fill="#e8f1f8" stroke="#1b6ca8" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="360" y="300" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#1b6ca8">Getting the best from a desiccant</text>
<text x="34" y="322" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">• keep the reactivation duct SHORT — long runs restrict airflow and can cool the air below dew point, filling the duct with water</text>
<text x="34" y="340" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">• duct the process inlet from the coolest, driest air available — cold air is drier, and it cools the hot rotor back to working temperature faster</text>
<text x="360" y="268" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="#d1491c">A three-hole desiccant ALWAYS creates a pressure differential in the environment</text>
</svg>

s1-electricity.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 380" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">
<rect width="720" height="380" fill="#fff"/>
<text x="360" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Electricity on the Drying Job</text>
<rect x="20" y="42" width="216" height="118" rx="8" fill="#e8f1f8" stroke="#1b6ca8" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="128" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#1b6ca8">VOLTAGE (volts)</text>
<text x="128" y="86" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">The force or “push” of the current</text>
<text x="128" y="108" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">US residential devices: 110–120 V</text>
<text x="128" y="130" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Ranges and clothes dryers: 220–240 V</text>
<text x="128" y="152" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Typical service: 230 V, 100–200 A</text>
<rect x="252" y="42" width="216" height="118" rx="8" fill="#fdf6e3" stroke="#c9a227" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="360" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#a5851f">AMPERAGE (amps)</text>
<text x="360" y="86" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">The amount of current flowing</text>
<text x="360" y="102" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">through a circuit at a moment</text>
<rect x="270" y="112" width="180" height="38" rx="5" fill="#d1491c"/>
<text x="360" y="128" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#fff">NEC: never more than 80%</text>
<text x="360" y="143" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#fff">continuously — 15 A → 12 A, 20 A → 16 A</text>
<rect x="484" y="42" width="216" height="118" rx="8" fill="#e7f3ec" stroke="#2e7d4f" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="592" y="64" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">WATTAGE (watts)</text>
<text x="592" y="86" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">The work electricity produces</text>
<text x="592" y="102" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">per second</text>
<rect x="502" y="112" width="180" height="38" rx="5" fill="#2e7d4f"/>
<text x="592" y="137" text-anchor="middle" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#fff">amps × volts = watts</text>
<rect x="20" y="174" width="340" height="92" rx="8" fill="#f7f9fb" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="190" y="196" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Generator sizing</text>
<text x="190" y="222" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">kW = (Ta × V) ÷ 1,000</text>
<text x="190" y="244" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">Ta = total amperage · V = voltage · 1,000 = watts per kW</text>
<text x="190" y="260" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#d1491c">The 80% rule applies to generators too</text>
<rect x="376" y="174" width="324" height="92" rx="8" fill="#fbeee9" stroke="#d1491c" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="538" y="196" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">Heat produced by equipment</text>
<text x="538" y="222" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">amps × volts × 3.4 = BTUs per hour</text>
<text x="538" y="244" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">12,000 BTU/h = one “ton” of heating or air conditioning</text>
<text x="538" y="260" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">Offset with the building AC, portable AC, or cool outdoor air</text>
<rect x="20" y="280" width="680" height="88" rx="8" fill="#e8f1f8" stroke="#1b6ca8" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="360" y="302" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#1b6ca8">Electrical cost for the customer</text>
<text x="360" y="328" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">amps × volts × 24 ÷ 1000 × cost per kWh = cost per day</text>
<text x="360" y="350" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">Rule of thumb: $1.00 to $1.50 per piece of drying equipment per day — normally a covered expense under insurance policies</text>
<text x="360" y="366" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">200 A at 230 V is equivalent to 400 A at 115 V</text>
</svg>

alt.en: Panels comparing surface, free and bound water with the drying conditions each needs

s1-three-forms-of-water.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 740 370" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">
<rect width="740" height="370" fill="#fff"/>
<text x="370" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Three Forms of Water in Materials</text>
<text x="370" y="46" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">Each form needs a different combination of airflow, temperature and humidity</text>
<g>
<rect x="16" y="60" width="230" height="240" rx="8" fill="#e7f3ec" stroke="#2e7d4f" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="16" y="60" width="230" height="30" rx="8" fill="#2e7d4f"/>
<text x="131" y="81" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#fff">SURFACE WATER</text>
<text x="131" y="110" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Readily available at the surface;</text>
<text x="131" y="126" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">liquid, visible, evaporates readily</text>
<text x="131" y="150" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">ALL materials can hold it</text>
<text x="131" y="176" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Best removed PHYSICALLY, with</text>
<text x="131" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">mechanical extraction equipment</text>
<text x="131" y="216" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">The rest evaporates with large</text>
<text x="131" y="232" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">airflow and MODERATE</text>
<text x="131" y="248" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">temperature and humidity</text>
<text x="131" y="274" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">FASTEST evaporation rate</text>
<text x="131" y="292" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">gone in the first several hours</text>
</g>
<g>
<rect x="256" y="60" width="230" height="240" rx="8" fill="#e8f1f8" stroke="#1b6ca8" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="256" y="60" width="230" height="30" rx="8" fill="#1b6ca8"/>
<text x="371" y="81" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#fff">FREE WATER</text>
<text x="371" y="110" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Within the material but NOT</text>
<text x="371" y="126" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">bonded — in cavities, open pores</text>
<text x="371" y="142" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">and air spaces; often visible as a</text>
<text x="371" y="158" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">darkening of the material</text>
<text x="371" y="182" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#1b6ca8">MOST materials can hold it</text>
<text x="371" y="198" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">not vinyl, VCT, steel, rubber or</text>
<text x="371" y="212" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">other solid synthetics</text>
<text x="371" y="238" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Needs sufficient airflow, WARM</text>
<text x="371" y="254" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">temperatures and MODERATELY</text>
<text x="371" y="270" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">LOW humidity</text>
<text x="371" y="292" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#1b6ca8">Evaporates quickly</text>
</g>
<g>
<rect x="496" y="60" width="228" height="240" rx="8" fill="#fbeee9" stroke="#d1491c" stroke-width="2"/>
<rect x="496" y="60" width="228" height="30" rx="8" fill="#d1491c"/>
<text x="610" y="81" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#fff">BOUND WATER</text>
<text x="610" y="110" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Absorbed and held captive by</text>
<text x="610" y="126" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">CHEMICAL BONDS — it must be</text>
<text x="610" y="142" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">freed before it can be removed</text>
<text x="610" y="168" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">AIRFLOW IS LEAST EFFECTIVE</text>
<text x="610" y="194" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Materials dry fastest when they</text>
<text x="610" y="210" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">are WARM and the surrounding</text>
<text x="610" y="226" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">humidity is VERY LOW</text>
<text x="610" y="252" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">Evaporates VERY SLOWLY</text>
<text x="610" y="276" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">Heat counteracts the chemical bond</text>
<text x="610" y="290" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">— but watch for secondary damage</text>
</g>
<rect x="16" y="312" width="708" height="48" rx="8" fill="#f7f9fb" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="370" y="333" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">A drying principle for ALL materials</text>
<text x="370" y="352" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">Wet items dry faster if DRIER AIR is supplied, with ADEQUATE AIRFLOW, at a GOOD DRYING TEMPERATURE</text>
</svg>

s1-hardwood-damage.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 360" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">
<rect width="720" height="360" fill="#fff"/>
<text x="360" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Hardwood — Milling, Cupping and Buckling</text>
<rect x="20" y="44" width="330" height="150" rx="8" fill="#e7f3ec" stroke="#2e7d4f" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="185" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">QUARTER SAWN (hardwood) / FLAT GRAINED (softwood)</text>
<rect x="60" y="80" width="230" height="46" fill="#e8d5b7" stroke="#12263a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<g stroke="#8a6a3d" stroke-width="1.6">
<line x1="80" y1="80" x2="80" y2="126"/><line x1="110" y1="80" x2="110" y2="126"/><line x1="140" y1="80" x2="140" y2="126"/>
<line x1="170" y1="80" x2="170" y2="126"/><line x1="200" y1="80" x2="200" y2="126"/><line x1="230" y1="80" x2="230" y2="126"/><line x1="260" y1="80" x2="260" y2="126"/>
</g>
<text x="185" y="148" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Annual rings make straight, parallel lines</text>
<text x="185" y="166" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">LESS dimensional change across the width;</text>
<text x="185" y="182" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">more resilient to visible changes such as warping</text>
<rect x="370" y="44" width="330" height="150" rx="8" fill="#fbeee9" stroke="#d1491c" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="535" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">PLAIN SAWN (hardwood) / EDGE GRAINED (softwood)</text>
<rect x="410" y="80" width="230" height="46" fill="#e8d5b7" stroke="#12263a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<g stroke="#8a6a3d" stroke-width="1.6" fill="none">
<path d="M430 126 q14 -23 0 -46"/><path d="M470 126 q22 -23 0 -46"/><path d="M510 126 q30 -23 0 -46"/>
<path d="M560 126 q-30 -23 0 -46"/><path d="M600 126 q-22 -23 0 -46"/>
</g>
<text x="535" y="148" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Rings form “flares” and a curved grain on the cut ends</text>
<text x="535" y="166" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Cheaper to produce, greater yield per log — but absorbs and</text>
<text x="535" y="182" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">releases moisture more readily and is MORE LIKELY TO WARP</text>
<rect x="20" y="208" width="215" height="136" rx="8" fill="#e8f1f8" stroke="#1b6ca8" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="127" y="230" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#1b6ca8">CUPPING</text>
<path d="M50 262 q77 -22 154 0 l0 18 q-77 -22 -154 0 z" fill="#e8d5b7" stroke="#12263a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="127" y="302" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">The bottom and sides absorb moisture,</text>
<text x="127" y="316" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">the bottom expands, the edges bend up</text>
<text x="127" y="336" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">NOT permanent — should be dried</text>
<rect x="247" y="208" width="215" height="136" rx="8" fill="#fbeee9" stroke="#d1491c" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="354" y="230" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">BUCKLING</text>
<path d="M277 280 l60 0 q40 -34 60 -2 l30 2 l0 14 l-30 -2 q-22 -28 -60 2 l-60 0 z" fill="#e8d5b7" stroke="#12263a" stroke-width="1.5"/>
<text x="354" y="308" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">Moisture migrates from the bottom to the</text>
<text x="354" y="322" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">top, the top expands, horizontal pressure</text>
<text x="354" y="338" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">Usually cannot be repaired — replace</text>
<rect x="474" y="208" width="226" height="136" rx="8" fill="#f7f9fb" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="587" y="230" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Moisture thresholds in wood</text>
<rect x="492" y="244" width="190" height="34" rx="5" fill="#d1491c"/>
<text x="587" y="266" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#fff">above 20% MC, extended time</text>
<text x="587" y="294" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">→ wood decaying fungi (rot)</text>
<rect x="492" y="302" width="190" height="28" rx="5" fill="#c9a227"/>
<text x="587" y="321" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#fff">near or above 16% MC</text>
<text x="587" y="344" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">→ surface fungi (Aspergillus, Penicillium)</text>
</svg>

caption.en: Engineered lumber — processing vs damage

s1-engineered-wood.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 740 340" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">
<rect width="740" height="340" fill="#fff"/>
<text x="370" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Engineered Lumber (“Was-Wood”) — Processing vs Damage</text>
<text x="370" y="46" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">The more the fibre has been processed and re-adhered, the more rapid and dramatic the effects of wetting</text>
<defs>
<linearGradient id="wg" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
<stop offset="0%" stop-color="#2e7d4f"/><stop offset="50%" stop-color="#c9a227"/><stop offset="100%" stop-color="#d1491c"/>
</linearGradient>
<marker id="ew" markerWidth="10" markerHeight="10" refX="8" refY="3" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L9,3 L0,6 z" fill="#d1491c"/></marker>
</defs>
<rect x="40" y="62" width="640" height="14" rx="7" fill="url(#wg)"/>
<line x1="680" y1="69" x2="702" y2="69" stroke="#d1491c" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#ew)"/>
<text x="60" y="94" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">LEAST engineered · most natural fibre bonding</text>
<text x="672" y="94" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">MOST adhesive · fastest, most permanent damage</text>
<g font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">
<rect x="24" y="106" width="140" height="130" rx="6" fill="#e7f3ec" stroke="#2e7d4f" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="94" y="128" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">PLYWOOD</text>
<text x="94" y="150" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">Wood veneer layers</text>
<text x="94" y="164" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">glued under extreme</text>
<text x="94" y="178" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">pressure; resistant to</text>
<text x="94" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">swelling and delamination</text>
<text x="94" y="216" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">subflooring, sheathing,</text>
<text x="94" y="228" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">base for engineered floors</text>
<rect x="172" y="106" width="128" height="130" rx="6" fill="#eef3ea" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="236" y="128" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#5d6a73">COM-PLY</text>
<text x="236" y="150" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">Veneer surface like</text>
<text x="236" y="164" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">plywood, but a core of</text>
<text x="236" y="178" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">much smaller fibres and</text>
<text x="236" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">much artificial adhesive</text>
<text x="236" y="216" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">greater potential for</text>
<text x="236" y="228" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">delamination · subflooring</text>
<rect x="308" y="106" width="128" height="130" rx="6" fill="#fdf6e3" stroke="#c9a227" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="372" y="128" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#a5851f">OSB and LVL</text>
<text x="372" y="150" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">OSB: large chips laminated</text>
<text x="372" y="164" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">into a sheet; LVL: strips</text>
<text x="372" y="178" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">laminated into dimensional</text>
<text x="372" y="192" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">lumber — water acts alike</text>
<text x="372" y="216" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">joists, sheathing, roofing,</text>
<text x="372" y="228" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">shear walls, studs, beams</text>
<rect x="444" y="106" width="128" height="130" rx="6" fill="#fbeee9" stroke="#d1491c" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="508" y="128" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">PARTICLE BOARD</text>
<text x="508" y="150" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">Even smaller fibre than</text>
<text x="508" y="164" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">OSB, and more adhesive</text>
<text x="508" y="188" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">underlayment for hard</text>
<text x="508" y="202" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">surface flooring</text>
<text x="508" y="224" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">normally removed</text>
<rect x="580" y="106" width="136" height="130" rx="6" fill="#f7ddd5" stroke="#d1491c" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<text x="648" y="128" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">MDF</text>
<text x="648" y="150" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">The SMALLEST natural</text>
<text x="648" y="164" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">fibre — comparable to</text>
<text x="648" y="178" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5">thick paper sheets</text>
<text x="648" y="200" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">Suffers the most rapid</text>
<text x="648" y="214" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">and permanent damage</text>
<text x="648" y="230" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">trim and baseboard</text>
</g>
<rect x="24" y="250" width="692" height="76" rx="8" fill="#f7f9fb" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="370" y="272" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Normally NOT restorable when damaged — these are removed</text>
<text x="370" y="294" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" fill="#d1491c" font-weight="bold">medium density fibreboard (MDF) · particle board · laminate flooring · parquet floors</text>
<text x="370" y="316" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="#555">Bamboo can be dried if the surface is undamaged; engineered hardwood can be dried but is often removed for surface damage</text>
</svg>

caption.ru: Если не сохнет — двигаться от наименее разрушающих мер
caption.en: If it is not drying — escalate from least disruptive

alt.ru: Две лестницы действий для полов и стен — от усиления потока до полного удаления
alt.en: Two escalation ladders for floors and walls, from more airflow to full removal

s1-drying-escalation.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 740 380" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">
<rect width="740" height="380" fill="#fff"/>
<text x="370" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">If It Is Not Drying — Escalate from LEAST Disruptive</text>
<text x="370" y="46" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">Evaporation increases as materials are made warmer, as air is made drier, and as air moves faster across the wet surface</text>
<rect x="20" y="60" width="340" height="300" rx="8" fill="#e8f1f8" stroke="#1b6ca8" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="190" y="84" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#1b6ca8">FLOORS</text>
<g font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">
<text x="38" y="112">1.  Add more direct airflow on the surface</text>
<text x="54" y="128">and subsurface of the floor</text>
<text x="38" y="154">2.  Provide drier air with desiccant</text>
<text x="54" y="170">dehumidification</text>
<text x="38" y="196">3.  Dry from both bottom and top</text>
<text x="54" y="212">(“sandwich drying”)</text>
<text x="38" y="238">4.  Feed air movers blowing into the floor</text>
<text x="54" y="254">with dehumidifiers</text>
<text x="38" y="280">5.  Warm floor surfaces with heat lamps</text>
<text x="38" y="306" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">6.  Remove wet flooring completely</text>
</g>
<text x="190" y="338" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">Wood floors: drying mats, injection systems,</text>
<text x="190" y="352" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">or tenting with warm dry air — or all three</text>
<rect x="380" y="60" width="340" height="300" rx="8" fill="#e7f3ec" stroke="#2e7d4f" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="550" y="84" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">WALLS</text>
<g font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">
<text x="398" y="108">1.  Add more direct airflow outside the wall</text>
<text x="398" y="132">2.  Move the dehumidifier output closer to</text>
<text x="414" y="146">the wet surface</text>
<text x="398" y="170">3.  Carefully remove baseboards, continue</text>
<text x="414" y="184">airflow along the outside of the wall</text>
<text x="398" y="208">4.  Drill holes below baseboard level to let</text>
<text x="414" y="222">the wall breathe</text>
<text x="398" y="246">5.  Blow direct airflow INTO the wall with air</text>
<text x="414" y="260">movers or inter-air dryers</text>
<text x="398" y="284">6.  Feed those air movers with a dehumidifier</text>
<text x="398" y="308">7.  Warm wall surfaces with direct heat</text>
<text x="398" y="332" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">8.  Completely remove all wet wallboard</text>
<text x="414" y="346" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">and all wet insulation</text>
</g>
</svg>

caption.en: Temperature limits of common materials and contents

caption.en: Drying crawlspaces

alt.ru: Правило разрежения с разрезом через жилую зону и подполье, прочие факторы и способы проверки
alt.en: The negative pressure rule with a section through living space and crawlspace, plus other factors and verification

s1-crawlspace-drying.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 360" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">
<rect width="720" height="360" fill="#fff"/>
<text x="360" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Drying Crawlspaces</text>
<rect x="30" y="44" width="660" height="44" rx="8" fill="#d1491c"/>
<text x="360" y="62" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#fff">THE NUMBER ONE SAFETY RULE</text>
<text x="360" y="80" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#fff">Always dry crawlspaces under a NEGATIVE pressure</text>
<defs><marker id="cs" markerWidth="10" markerHeight="10" refX="8" refY="3" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L9,3 L0,6 z" fill="#d1491c"/></marker></defs>
<rect x="60" y="104" width="290" height="60" fill="#eef3f7" stroke="#12263a" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="205" y="140" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">LIVING SPACE</text>
<rect x="60" y="164" width="290" height="10" fill="#12263a"/>
<rect x="60" y="174" width="290" height="56" fill="#fbeee9" stroke="#12263a" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="205" y="198" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">CRAWLSPACE</text>
<text x="205" y="218" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">dust, mould spores, dead insects or worse</text>
<line x1="205" y1="170" x2="205" y2="140" stroke="#d1491c" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#cs)" stroke-dasharray="6,4"/>
<text x="240" y="160" font-size="10.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">what POSITIVE pressure would do</text>
<line x1="56" y1="202" x2="20" y2="202" stroke="#2e7d4f" stroke-width="3"/>
<text x="205" y="248" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Remove MORE air (CFM) than is added → negative pressure</text>
<text x="205" y="264" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">Verify with a manometer</text>
<rect x="376" y="104" width="314" height="160" rx="8" fill="#e8f1f8" stroke="#1b6ca8" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="533" y="126" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#1b6ca8">Other important factors</text>
<text x="392" y="150" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">• crawlspaces are dangerous — follow all safety rules</text>
<text x="392" y="172" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">• use submersible pumps; in dirt crawlspaces dig a</text>
<text x="404" y="186" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">shallow hole so the pump can reach a deeper level</text>
<text x="392" y="208" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">• for dehumidifiers, measure the OUTSIDE of the</text>
<text x="404" y="222" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">structure × average crawlspace height for cubic feet</text>
<text x="392" y="244" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">• heat has fewer limits in unoccupied spaces — use</text>
<text x="404" y="258" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">warmer outdoor air to promote evaporation</text>
<rect x="30" y="280" width="660" height="66" rx="8" fill="#e7f3ec" stroke="#2e7d4f" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="360" y="302" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">Verifying that the system is working</text>
<text x="360" y="322" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">Dehumidifiers — document performance using GRAIN DEPRESSION</text>
<text x="360" y="340" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">Heat drying — compare the negative air output (exhaust) with the outdoor air; the difference in humidity ratio shows what is being removed</text>
</svg>

caption.ru: Обследование и мониторинг, и три вещи для документирования
caption.en: Inspection vs monitoring, and the three things to document

alt.en: Two panels comparing inspection and monitoring, plus meter, location and method documentation

s1-monitoring-consistency.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 360" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">
<rect width="720" height="360" fill="#fff"/>
<text x="360" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Inspection vs Monitoring — and the Three Things to Document</text>
<rect x="20" y="44" width="330" height="86" rx="8" fill="#e8f1f8" stroke="#1b6ca8" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="185" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#1b6ca8">INSPECTION</text>
<text x="185" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">Gathering data to accurately evaluate</text>
<text x="185" y="108" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">the CURRENT condition</text>
<rect x="370" y="44" width="330" height="86" rx="8" fill="#e7f3ec" stroke="#2e7d4f" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="535" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">MONITORING</text>
<text x="535" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">A series of REPEATED inspections to</text>
<text x="535" y="108" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">evaluate and document CHANGE</text>
<text x="360" y="152" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">“Repeated” is the key word — conduct inspections the same way each time</text>
<rect x="20" y="166" width="222" height="120" rx="8" fill="#f7f9fb" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="131" y="188" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">DOCUMENT THE METER</text>
<text x="131" y="212" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Meters vary greatly between</text>
<text x="131" y="228" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">makers and models</text>
<text x="131" y="252" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">Two inspections of the same</text>
<text x="131" y="268" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">material with different models</text>
<text x="131" y="282" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">give entirely different readings</text>
<rect x="250" y="166" width="222" height="120" rx="8" fill="#f7f9fb" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="361" y="188" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">DOCUMENT THE LOCATION</text>
<text x="361" y="212" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Moisture levels fluctuate across</text>
<text x="361" y="228" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">a surface and at varying depths</text>
<text x="361" y="254" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Removable coloured dot stickers</text>
<text x="361" y="270" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">and painter’s masking tape keep</text>
<text x="361" y="284" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">monitoring consistent</text>
<rect x="480" y="166" width="220" height="120" rx="8" fill="#f7f9fb" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="590" y="188" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">DOCUMENT THE METHOD</text>
<text x="590" y="212" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Note where a measurement</text>
<text x="590" y="228" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">BEGINS — from the carpet</text>
<text x="590" y="244" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">surface or the top of the</text>
<text x="590" y="260" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">baseboard — not just how high</text>
<text x="590" y="282" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="#555">mark it at the inspection point too</text>
<rect x="20" y="298" width="680" height="52" rx="8" fill="#fbeee9" stroke="#d1491c" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="360" y="318" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">Readings from different technologies and different makers CANNOT be compared</text>
<text x="360" y="338" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">One non-invasive model may use a scale of 1 to 20 and another 1 to 999 — the values mean nothing to each other</text>
</svg>

s1-dot-system.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 700 330" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">
<rect width="700" height="330" fill="#fff"/>
<text x="350" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">The Dot System</text>
<text x="350" y="46" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">Removable coloured stickers showing the relative amount of moisture, or the intended procedure</text>
<g>
<circle cx="70" cy="86" r="20" fill="#2e7d4f"/>
<text x="105" y="82" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">GREEN</text>
<text x="105" y="100" font-size="12" fill="#12263a">Within acceptable tolerance of the dry standard</text>
<circle cx="70" cy="140" r="20" fill="#c9a227"/>
<text x="105" y="136" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#a5851f">YELLOW</text>
<text x="105" y="154" font-size="12" fill="#12263a">Abnormally wet but not saturated — at risk for secondary damage</text>
<circle cx="70" cy="194" r="20" fill="#d1491c"/>
<text x="105" y="190" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">RED</text>
<text x="105" y="208" font-size="12" fill="#12263a">Near saturation — high risk for secondary damage</text>
<circle cx="70" cy="248" r="20" fill="#1b6ca8"/>
<text x="105" y="244" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#1b6ca8">BLUE</text>
<text x="105" y="262" font-size="12" fill="#12263a">Material scheduled for REMOVAL</text>
</g>
<rect x="20" y="278" width="660" height="42" rx="8" fill="#e8f1f8" stroke="#1b6ca8" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="350" y="297" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#1b6ca8">With the dot system the technician tracks the SIZE of the wet area (“what is wet?”), not the actual moisture level (“how wet is it?”)</text>
<text x="350" y="314" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Measure from the floor surface to the dot and record the height; date or number the dots, since many are used over the course of drying</text>
</svg>

s1-adjusting-drying.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 360" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">
<rect width="720" height="360" fill="#fff"/>
<text x="360" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Adjusting the Drying Method After Each Day</text>
<text x="360" y="46" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-style="italic" fill="#555">After 24 hours (or less) of drying, materials are re-inspected and the approach is adjusted</text>
<rect x="16" y="62" width="222" height="110" rx="8" fill="#e7f3ec" stroke="#2e7d4f" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="127" y="86" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">MATERIAL IS DRYING</text>
<text x="127" y="112" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">Continue with the current</text>
<text x="127" y="128" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">drying approach</text>
<text x="127" y="152" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="#555">it is working and progress is being made</text>
<rect x="248" y="62" width="222" height="110" rx="8" fill="#e8f1f8" stroke="#1b6ca8" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="359" y="86" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#1b6ca8">MATERIAL HAS DRIED</text>
<text x="359" y="112" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">Reposition equipment to focus</text>
<text x="359" y="128" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">on other areas, or remove it</text>
<text x="359" y="152" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="#555">the drying goal has been achieved</text>
<rect x="480" y="62" width="224" height="110" rx="8" fill="#fbeee9" stroke="#d1491c" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="592" y="86" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">MATERIAL IS NOT DRYING</text>
<text x="592" y="112" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">MODIFY the approach — change</text>
<text x="592" y="128" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">the equipment or the material,</text>
<text x="592" y="144" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">whichever is more economical</text>
<text x="592" y="164" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="#555">it is not working</text>
<text x="360" y="196" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">When it is not drying, re-evaluate the material on three counts</text>
<rect x="16" y="208" width="222" height="98" rx="8" fill="#f7f9fb" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="127" y="230" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">CONTAMINATION</text>
<text x="127" y="254" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">After another 24 hours wet, is</text>
<text x="127" y="270" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">there now a concern? Can it be</text>
<text x="127" y="286" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">treated, or must it be removed?</text>
<rect x="248" y="208" width="222" height="98" rx="8" fill="#f7f9fb" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="359" y="230" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#a5851f">DAMAGE</text>
<text x="359" y="254" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Has permanent secondary</text>
<text x="359" y="270" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">damage appeared — warping,</text>
<text x="359" y="286" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">swelling, splitting, staining?</text>
<rect x="480" y="208" width="224" height="98" rx="8" fill="#f7f9fb" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="592" y="230" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">COST</text>
<text x="592" y="254" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">The system is not working and</text>
<text x="592" y="270" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">must change — which costs less,</text>
<text x="592" y="286" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">removal or more equipment?</text>
<rect x="16" y="316" width="688" height="36" rx="6" fill="#e8f1f8" stroke="#1b6ca8" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="360" y="339" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">Drying goals may be set equal to the dry standard, or within 10% of the dry standard or normal equilibrium moisture content (EMC)</text>
</svg>

s1-grain-depression.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 350" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">
<rect width="720" height="350" fill="#fff"/>
<text x="360" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Grain Depression — and Where It Belongs in the Picture</text>
<defs><marker id="gd" markerWidth="10" markerHeight="10" refX="8" refY="3" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L9,3 L0,6 z" fill="#12263a"/></marker></defs>
<rect x="30" y="48" width="150" height="54" rx="6" fill="#fbeee9" stroke="#d1491c" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="105" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">AIR ENTERING</text>
<text x="105" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">higher GPP</text>
<rect x="220" y="42" width="140" height="66" rx="6" fill="#12263a"/>
<text x="290" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#fff">DEHUMIDIFIER</text>
<text x="290" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#fff">processes the air</text>
<rect x="400" y="48" width="150" height="54" rx="6" fill="#e7f3ec" stroke="#2e7d4f" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="475" y="70" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#2e7d4f">AIR PROCESSED</text>
<text x="475" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">lower GPP</text>
<line x1="184" y1="75" x2="214" y2="75" stroke="#12263a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#gd)"/>
<line x1="364" y1="75" x2="394" y2="75" stroke="#12263a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#gd)"/>
<text x="620" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">GRAIN</text>
<text x="620" y="82" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">DEPRESSION</text>
<text x="620" y="100" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" font-style="italic" fill="#d1491c">minimal GD = poor performance</text>
<rect x="30" y="120" width="300" height="72" rx="8" fill="#e8f1f8" stroke="#1b6ca8" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="180" y="142" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#1b6ca8">Converting to water removed</text>
<text x="180" y="168" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">P = CFM × GD ÷ 71</text>
<text x="180" y="186" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">P = pints per 24 hours · 71 consolidates the constants</text>
<rect x="346" y="120" width="344" height="72" rx="8" fill="#fdf6e3" stroke="#c9a227" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="518" y="142" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#a5851f">Metric equivalent</text>
<text x="518" y="168" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Litres per day = CMH × GD ÷ 33</text>
<text x="518" y="186" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">Grain depression alone ignores how much air each unit processes</text>
<rect x="30" y="206" width="660" height="132" rx="8" fill="#f7f9fb" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="360" y="228" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Judge the job in this order — never on grain depression alone</text>
<rect x="48" y="240" width="200" height="42" rx="5" fill="#2e7d4f"/>
<text x="148" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#fff">1. MOISTURE IN MATERIALS</text>
<text x="148" y="274" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#fff">evaluate first, most attention</text>
<rect x="260" y="240" width="200" height="42" rx="5" fill="#1b6ca8"/>
<text x="360" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#fff">2. HUMIDITY AND TEMPERATURE</text>
<text x="360" y="274" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#fff">of the air used to dry them</text>
<rect x="472" y="240" width="200" height="42" rx="5" fill="#c9a227"/>
<text x="572" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#fff">3. MECHANICAL SYSTEMS</text>
<text x="572" y="274" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#fff">HVAC plus portable dehumidifiers</text>
<text x="360" y="304" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">If materials are drying, the system as a whole is performing — including the dehumidification</text>
<text x="360" y="324" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">Basing decisions solely on grain depression will lead to false determinations</text>
</svg>

s1-mold-timeline.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 340" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">
<rect width="720" height="340" fill="#fff"/>
<text x="360" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">How Long Does Mould Really Take to Grow?</text>
<line x1="60" y1="120" x2="680" y2="120" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<g font-size="11" fill="#12263a">
<line x1="110" y1="112" x2="110" y2="128" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="110" y="146" text-anchor="middle">a few hours</text>
<line x1="240" y1="112" x2="240" y2="128" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="240" y="146" text-anchor="middle">24–48 hours</text>
<line x1="380" y1="112" x2="380" y2="128" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="380" y="146" text-anchor="middle">3 days (72 h)</text>
<line x1="500" y1="112" x2="500" y2="128" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="500" y="146" text-anchor="middle">4 days (96 h)</text>
<line x1="640" y1="112" x2="640" y2="128" stroke="#7a8791" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="640" y="146" text-anchor="middle">weeks</text>
</g>
<text x="110" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">spores germinate</text>
<text x="110" y="80" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">in the lab</text>
<rect x="180" y="64" width="120" height="40" rx="5" fill="#fdf6e3" stroke="#c9a227"/>
<text x="240" y="80" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">EPA: respond to</text>
<text x="240" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">clean water in 24–48 h</text>
<text x="380" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">first tiny VISIBLE</text>
<text x="380" y="80" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">colonies of fast types</text>
<text x="500" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">colonies large enough</text>
<text x="500" y="80" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">to identify and count</text>
<text x="640" y="94" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">slow-growing types;</text>
<text x="640" y="80" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10.5" fill="#12263a">controlled-study results</text>
<rect x="20" y="166" width="330" height="76" rx="8" fill="#fdf6e3" stroke="#c9a227" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="185" y="188" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#a5851f">What the EPA says</text>
<text x="185" y="210" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">Respond to clean water damage within 24–48 hours</text>
<text x="185" y="228" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="#12263a">“Even if materials are dried within 48 hours,</text>
<text x="185" y="240" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-style="italic" fill="#12263a">mould growth may have occurred”</text>
<rect x="370" y="166" width="330" height="76" rx="8" fill="#e8f1f8" stroke="#1b6ca8" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="535" y="188" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#1b6ca8">The Krause controlled study</text>
<text x="535" y="210" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">On wet untreated wallboard in a closed office,</text>
<text x="535" y="226" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">at least a WEEK passed before hyphae were</text>
<text x="535" y="240" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" fill="#12263a">confirmed; visible colonies only at THREE WEEKS</text>
<rect x="20" y="256" width="680" height="70" rx="8" fill="#fbeee9" stroke="#d1491c" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="360" y="278" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="bold" fill="#d1491c">Always note musty odours — but do NOT assume mould is growing simply because 48 hours have passed</text>
<text x="360" y="300" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">Different species colonise at different rates, and the time required is affected by different climates and different food sources</text>
<text x="360" y="318" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">The best prevention remains drying all materials thoroughly and rapidly — no other procedure is as effective</text>
</svg>

s1-water-activity.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 720 360" font-family="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">
<rect width="720" height="360" fill="#fff"/>
<text x="360" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-size="17" font-weight="bold" fill="#12263a">Water Activity (aₐ) and Microbial Growth</text>
<rect x="20" y="44" width="330" height="128" rx="8" fill="#e8f1f8" stroke="#1b6ca8" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="185" y="66" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12.5" font-weight="bold" fill="#1b6ca8">MOISTURE CONTENT (MC)</text>
<text x="185" y="90" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">The amount of moisture at a SPECIFIC</text>
<text x="185" y="106" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11.5" fill="#12263a">LOCATION in a material</text>

question.ru: Что, согласно руководству, делает воду уникальной среди природных веществ?
question.en: What makes water unique among natural substances, according to the manual?

hint.ru: Подумайте о температурах, которые встречаются на Земле естественным образом, и о состояниях, которые вода принимает в этом диапазоне.
hint.en: Think about the temperature range that occurs naturally on earth and the states water can take within it.

text.ru: Это единственное природное вещество, встречающееся во всех трёх состояниях — жидком, твёрдом и газообразном — при температурах, обычных для Земли
text.en: It is the only natural substance found in all three states — liquid, solid and gas — at temperatures normally found on earth

explanation.ru: Верно — именно на эту уникальность указывает руководство.
explanation.en: Correct — this is exactly the uniqueness the manual points to.

text.ru: Это единственное вещество, которое не растворяет другие материалы
text.en: It is the only substance that does not dissolve other materials

explanation.ru: Неверно — в руководстве сказано, что вода способна растворять материалы.
explanation.en: Incorrect — the manual states water has the ability to dissolve materials.

text.ru: Это единственное вещество, не обладающее связующими свойствами
text.en: It is the only substance that has no bonding properties

explanation.ru: Неверно — вода описана как обладающая сильными связующими свойствами.
explanation.en: Incorrect — water is described as having strong bonding properties.

text.ru: Это единственное вещество, покрывающее более 90 % поверхности Земли
text.en: It is the only substance that covers more than 90% of the earth's surface

explanation.ru: Неверно — приведена цифра примерно 70 %, а не более 90 %.
explanation.en: Incorrect — the figure given is approximately 70%, not more than 90%.

text.ru: Все варианты верны
text.en: All of the above are correct

explanation.ru: Неверно — тексту соответствует только вариант 1.
explanation.en: Incorrect — only option 1 matches the text.

text.ru: Среди вариантов нет правильного ответа
text.en: There is no correct answer among the options

explanation.ru: Неверно — вариант 1 верен.
explanation.en: Incorrect — option 1 is correct.

explanation.ru: Вода встречается в виде жидкости, льда и пара в обычном земном диапазоне температур — ни одно другое природное вещество на это не способно. При этом она обладает сильными связующими свойствами, растворяет материалы и покрывает около 70 % поверхности, поэтому варианты 2, 3 и 4 противоречат тексту.
explanation.en: Water occurs as liquid, ice and vapour within the ordinary earthly temperature range — no other natural substance does. It also has strong bonding properties, dissolves materials and covers about 70% of the surface, so options 2, 3 and 4 contradict the text.

question.ru: Когда происходит залив, какой единственный фактор важнее всего определяет размер возможного ущерба?
question.en: When a water loss occurs, what is the single most critical factor in defining the amount of potential damage?

hint.ru: Руководство говорит, что все остальные уроки книги опираются на этот принцип — и именно он объясняет, почему важна скорость.
hint.en: The manual says every other lesson in the book pivots on this one principle — and it explains why speed matters.

text.ru: Объём воды, попавшей в здание
text.en: The volume of water that entered the structure

explanation.ru: Неверно — объём имеет значение, но текст выделяет именно время, а не объём.
explanation.en: Incorrect — volume matters, but the text singles out time, not volume.

text.ru: Время, в течение которого здание остаётся аномально влажным
text.en: The amount of time the structure remains abnormally wet

explanation.ru: Верно — это и есть названный самым критичным фактор.
explanation.en: Correct — this is the stated single most critical factor.

text.ru: Возраст здания и тип его фундамента
text.en: The age of the building and the type of its foundation

explanation.ru: Неверно — в этом фрагменте не назван критичным фактором.
explanation.en: Incorrect — not named as the critical factor in this passage.

text.ru: Количество сушильных машин, имеющихся у подрядчика
text.en: The number of drying machines available to the contractor

explanation.ru: Неверно — наличие оборудования не определяет размер ущерба.
explanation.en: Incorrect — equipment availability is not the defining factor of damage.

text.ru: Верны варианты 1 и 2
text.en: Options 1 and 2 are correct

explanation.ru: Неверно — вопрос о единственном самом критичном факторе.
explanation.en: Incorrect — the question asks for the single most critical factor.

text.ru: Все варианты верны
text.en: All of the above are correct

explanation.ru: Неверно — в тексте назван только вариант 2.
explanation.en: Incorrect — only option 2 is the stated answer.

explanation.ru: Руководство прямо указывает, что время, проведённое зданием во влажном состоянии, — самый критичный фактор. Именно поэтому важнейшее первое действие — быстро отреагировать и как можно скорее начать работы по уменьшению ущерба.
explanation.en: The manual states plainly that time wet is the single most critical factor. That is why the most critical initial course of action is to respond quickly and begin mitigation as soon as possible.

question.ru: Какое утверждение об ураганах и ущербе от воды соответствует руководству?
question.en: Which statement about hurricanes and water damage matches the manual?

hint.ru: Ураганы лидируют по стоимости ущерба, но повседневные отказы в зданиях лидируют по количеству случаев.
hint.en: Hurricanes dominate the cost tables, but everyday building failures dominate the case load.

text.ru: Ураганы дают восемь из десяти самых дорогих катастроф, когда-либо зафиксированных в Северной Америке, но при этом они не являются главной причиной проникновения воды в здания
text.en: Hurricanes account for eight of the ten most costly catastrophes ever recorded in North America, yet they are not the leading cause of water intrusion in structures

explanation.ru: Верно — обе части утверждения есть в тексте.
explanation.en: Correct — both halves of the statement are in the text.

text.ru: Ураганы — и самые дорогие катастрофы, и главная причина проникновения воды в здания
text.en: Hurricanes are both the most costly catastrophes and the leading cause of water intrusion in structures

explanation.ru: Неверно — руководство прямо отрицает, что ураганы лидируют среди причин проникновения воды.
explanation.en: Incorrect — the manual explicitly denies that hurricanes lead the causes of intrusion.

text.ru: Ураганы редко попадают в число самых дорогих катастроф Северной Америки
text.en: Hurricanes rarely appear among the costliest catastrophes in North America

explanation.ru: Неверно — сказано обратное.
explanation.en: Incorrect — the opposite is stated.

text.ru: Ущерб от воды при ураганах не входит в сферу восстановительной сушки
text.en: Water damage from hurricanes is excluded from the scope of restorative drying

explanation.ru: Неверно — процесс восстановительной сушки применяется при многих формах проникновения воды.
explanation.en: Incorrect — the restorative drying process is used for many forms of water intrusion.

text.ru: Верны варианты 2 и 4
text.en: Options 2 and 4 are correct

explanation.ru: Неверно — оба этих утверждения противоречат тексту.
explanation.en: Incorrect — both of those statements contradict the text.

text.ru: Среди вариантов нет правильного ответа
text.en: There is no correct answer among the options

explanation.ru: Неверно — вариант 1 верен.
explanation.en: Incorrect — option 1 is correct.

explanation.ru: Руководство приводит оба факта: ураганы дают восемь из десяти самых дорогих катастроф Северной Америки, и при этом избыточная влага в зданиях возникает главным образом из-за строительных дефектов, отказов сантехники, повреждений при замерзании и ненадлежащего обслуживания.
explanation.en: The manual gives both facts: hurricanes account for eight of the ten costliest North American catastrophes, and yet excessive moisture in buildings arises mainly from construction defects, plumbing failures, freeze damage and improper maintenance.

question.ru: Из каких четырёх элементов состоит процесс восстановительной сушки в определении руководства?
question.en: Which four elements make up the restorative drying process as the manual defines it?

hint.ru: Два из четырёх происходят до включения любого оборудования, а один признаёт, что спасти можно не всё.
hint.en: Two of the four happen before any equipment is switched on, and one of them accepts that not everything can be saved.

text.ru: Оценка, документирование, управляемая сушка и выборочная замена
text.en: Assessment, documentation, controlled drying and selective replacement

explanation.ru: Верно — это определение приведено в тексте.
explanation.en: Correct — this is the definition given in the text.

text.ru: Извлечение воды, демонтаж, реконструкция и выставление счёта
text.en: Extraction, demolition, reconstruction and invoicing

explanation.ru: Неверно — это отдельные работы, а не определённый в тексте процесс.
explanation.en: Incorrect — these are activities, not the defined process.

text.ru: Обследование, дезинфекция, устранение запаха и покраска
text.en: Inspection, disinfection, deodorisation and painting

explanation.ru: Неверно — это относится к другим видам восстановительных работ.
explanation.en: Incorrect — these belong to other parts of restoration work.

text.ru: Составление сметы, согласование, сушка и подписание акта клиентом
text.en: Estimation, negotiation, drying and client sign-off

explanation.ru: Неверно — коммерческие шаги не входят в это определение.
explanation.en: Incorrect — commercial steps are not part of this definition.

text.ru: Верны варианты 1 и 3
text.en: Options 1 and 3 are correct

explanation.ru: Неверно — вариант 3 не входит в определение.
explanation.en: Incorrect — option 3 is not part of the definition.

text.ru: Все варианты верны
text.en: All of the above are correct

explanation.ru: Неверно — тексту соответствует только вариант 1.
explanation.en: Incorrect — only option 1 matches the text.

explanation.ru: Руководство называет четыре элемента восстановительной сушки: оценка, документирование, управляемая сушка и выборочная замена; этот процесс применяется при многих формах проникновения воды.
explanation.en: The manual names the four elements of restorative drying as assessment, documentation, controlled drying and selective replacement, and notes this process is used to recover from many forms of water intrusion.

question.ru: Какой документ назван стандартом должной практики для профессии восстановления после ущерба от воды?
question.en: Which document is named as the standard of care for the water restoration profession?

hint.ru: Он разработан самой отраслью восстановления; у него есть «сестринский» документ по плесени.
